Marcus Thorne I was born into this word in a quiet farming town called Herringsdale from a human father and mother. Their names where Thomas and Clara Thorne. They where good parents that treated me well and wanted what was best for me. My mother and father taught me their trade at a young age so I could help run the family store. Said trade was making natural remedies that where popular with the local farmers and I enjoyed the feeling that helping the sick and wounded gave me. The most disturbing things we ever had to treat was when some poor, overconfident sod wandered too close to a place we locals called "The Elder Grove". It was located deep in the forest that neighboured our town and all the locals knew to steer clear of it. You see, the rumours where that this part of the forest was an ancient passageway that connected our world with that of the fey. No one really knew this for certain however. Since most people that wandered too close to it either returned a raving lunatic, or not at all. This man did however. He was an outsider that had heard rumours about the grove and the rare herbs that supposedly grew inside and filled with hubris ventured in, and payed the price. We did all we could to save him, but in the end there was nothing we could do except make his journey into the afterlife as painless as possible. There was one thing that stuck in my mind from that night however. In the midst of his ramblings he stopped and I saw a sudden flash of clearity in his eyes as he said, "The lady of the grove guards the water lily. The lily of soothing, the lily of renewal, the lily of rebirth. Don't trust her lies.." As years went by I grew into a young adult. I was 25 years old at this point and had become a hardworking and well liked man while tending to the shop with my parents. I liked my life and would've been satisfied if I could've spent the rest of it like this. But that wasn't to be. During spring that year my mother grew sick. Me and my father tried everything we knew to help her, but nothing seemed to help. It grew progressively worse every day until one summer morning, she didn't even have the strength to get out of bed anymore. That night while I was laying in my bed, I remembered something. The man we had tried to save all those years ago, didn't he mention that there was a water lily in the grove? Didn't he call it "The lily of renewal"? It was worth a shot! After all, we had run out of options. I waited for my parents to fall asleep and promptly snuck out of the house and journeyed into the forest. While walking in the forest I remarked on how eerie it was. I mean, I had walked in that forest probably hundreds of times but something about being there in the pitch black made my skin crawl. After what felt like hours, I finally reached the edge of the grove. Around the edge stood trees that looked like they could've been there longer than the forest itself, lined with vines and thorns so thick that I had to crawl to even have a chance to get through.

The inside of the grove was beautiful, a strange contrast to how eerie the forest had been on my walk there. There where big lush green trees and plantlife, ripe fruits that I didn't even recognize and it was all illuminated by moonlight. Finally I reached a small lake. I knelt down at the edge of it, looking at my reflection in the water. The water was remarkably clear, almost like looking straight into a mirror. All off a sudden I saw something in the water beside my own bewildered expression. It was another face, the face of a woman. I quickly realised that what I was seeing wasn't a womans face in the water at all, it was her reflection. I spun around to see a tall beautiful woman with long white hair, golden skin and deep amber eyes. She wore a dress made out of leaves and flowers and her hair was covered in what looked like gleaming stones and gems. "Wh-what are u?", I stuttered. "What am I? My, my, that's no way to treat a lady dearie! U should start by asking her name or maybe complimenting her hair. You'll never find love behaving like that, u know. But if u must know, I am of the fey which I think u might've been able to guess seeing how you've wandered into this place. And the name's Lyra, by the way. What's yours handsome?", she said while giving me a sly wink. "I-it's Marcus", I said. "Well Marcus, I'm guessing you haven't come all this way just to see little ol' me. So go on, what have you come for dearie?", she said as her deep amber eyes felt like they where staring into my very soul. "M-my mother is very sick, and I've heard that there's a flower here that might be able to help her. A water lily.", I said. "I see, I see, but you know dearie that flower is very precious to me. So I can't just give it away...But it just so happens that I've had a fabulous idea! I'll give u the flower, right here and now. But in return, you have to get something for me. Deal?" I didn't hesitate for a second "Deal", I said. "Splendid, now just a little kiss to seal the deal.", she said while leaning forward. I met her half way and kissed her. But as soon as my lips touched hers It felt like molten metal was pouring down my throat. I fell to the ground writhing in pain and fear as I watched my skin and hair turn a sickly green colour and a crown of brambles began to grow out of my head. After what felt like an eternity of pain I heard Lyra's voice through the blur of everything that was happening to me. "Oh, don't worry. This is just a necessary thing for you to be able to give what you promised me. Oh my, I'm so sorry. I never told you what it was you where giving me in return did I? Well to be fair, you never asked." My eyes widened. "U see dearie, being stuck here all the time can get awfully drab and I've always wanted a son. And as it would seem I've now found one, namely you." I tried to scream but no words came out, just pain. "Oh don't worry, the transformation will take years to develop fully so in the meantime why don't you travel the world? You know, see new places, meet new people and grow stronger and while you're at it, bring your dear mother some entertainment." "And as the kind and caring mother that I am I'll even give you a friend to keep you company!" She said and gestured to a black raven that had just landed on her shoulder. "A mother has to keep a close eye on her children or else they might get rebellious when left to their own devices. And we can't have that, can we dearie?" She laughed and snapped her fingers, and everything went black but for a moment I swore I could see her previously beautiful form turn crooked and horrible. "Don't disappoint, dearie..."
- As I woke up in the forest and inspected myself I found that what I at first thought must've just been a very bad dream, was in fact real.
